paragraphs: The 120i has been part of the 1 Series range since 2011, and across its two generations has used three different engines — from the early N13 and N20 through to today's B48. The early F20/F21 generation (2011–2015) used the N13 (1.6-litre turbo) in some markets and the N20 (2.0-litre turbo) in others, with the N20 known for a well-documented timing chain guide issue. From 2015, the F20/F21 switched to the B48 — a newer 2.0-litre turbo unit that's significantly more reliable — and the F40 generation (2019–present) continues with the B48. The full breakdown by engine code is below. The 120i is no longer in production in some markets, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the 120i in some markets from 2011 to 2015 (F20/F21). No major known issue pattern confirmed for this specific application.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the 120i from 2011 to 2015 (F20/F21). Known for timing chain guide failure — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder petrol engine fitted from 2015 onwards (F20/F21) and continuing into the F40 generation (2019–present). This is the current engine for the 120i and is generally more reliable than the earlier N20, with no major confirmed pattern of the same timing chain issue.

compatibility.intro: Because the 120i spans three engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N13, N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 120i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
